angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 424,377 km at 108.22 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.2401 +/- 0.0153 mas (same row, RUWE 0.93): 108.22 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.61 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-152 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract): 424,377 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.63 +/- 0.01 solar masses from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-152 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4044 +/- 34 K from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-152 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-152 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-152.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.667, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
